rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.9 and 3 - two-season (2016-17, 2017-18) randomized block field experiment in a farmer's field at Gosaba, West Bengal, five irrigation treatments, four replicates. Q2: Table 4 / Section 3.2 - fruit yield 56.51 t/ha under drip 100% ET0 and 53.00 t/ha under drip 80% ET0 versus 43.37 t/ha under surface irrigation, with the highest yield (61.67 t/ha) under drip 80% ET0 + straw mulch; the trial is in a dry-season water-short coastal saline setting. Q4: Table 9 / Section 3.7 - post-harvest soil EC was highest under surface irrigation and lowest under drip (0-15 cm: 3.61 vs 2.13-2.48 dS/m), which the authors link to reduced salinity stress for the crop; Table 12 reports soil water balance components (profile contribution, irrigation, effective rainfall, total water use) per treatment.
rows.notes: Single site, single tomato cultivar, plot scale (4 m x 3 m), two seasons. The 'drought conditions' in the passage map to dry-season water shortage due to salinity in the study; this is an approximate rather than exact match. Yield means presented with DMRT letters only, no SD/SE/CI. The only stated restriction (EC reduction confined to top-soil) concerns the salinity result, not yield. Q4 answered yes on the basis of measured soil salinity, the key stressor in this system; in-season root-zone soil moisture was not measured and the 'optimal soil moisture regime' mechanism is asserted from literature.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.9 and 3 - two-season replicated field experiment with five irrigation/mulch treatments. Q2: Table 4 / Section 3.2 and Abstract - drip irrigation at 80% ET0 + straw mulch gave the significantly highest fruit yield (61.67 t/ha) and marketable yield (60.32 t/ha), versus 43.37 t/ha for surface irrigation and 52.33 t/ha for surface + mulch. Q4: Table 9 / Section 3.7 - lowest post-harvest soil EC under drip 80% ET0 + mulch and highest under surface irrigation, linked by the authors to reduced salinity stress; Table 5 shows higher leaf N, K and chlorophyll under drip + mulch; Table 12 reports soil water balance components by treatment.
rows.notes: The passage names drip with straw mulch, which matches the study's best treatment exactly. Single site and cultivar, plot scale, two seasons; yield means given with DMRT letters only, no SD/SE/CI. The stated restriction that the EC and microbial benefits were confined to the top-soil layer concerns those outcomes rather than yield. Q4 yes rests on measured soil salinity as the intermediate variable; in-season soil moisture was not measured.
